09:25 Local Time, 03:55 GMT: India dominated a truncated second day's play to take control of the Colombo Test. If Day 1 belonged to Devdutt Padikkal, it was Dhruv Jurel's turn to shine as he raised his second Test hundred. Asked to bat a few overs before stumps - Sri Lanka stumbled in the dark and were reduced to 8 for 2 when bad light called a halt to the proceedings. The pitch has seam movement on offer for the packers while the spinners have areas to exploit. It's the moving day of this Test and Sri Lanka's hopes rest on their fragile middle-order and Sonal Dinusha, their best batter in the Galle Test. We start at 9:45 am to make up for some of the time lost yesterday.
09:35 Local Time, 04:05 GMT: It's a bright and sunny morning in Colombo. The Indians are warming-up and we should've a prompt start

Pitch report [Russel Arnold]: Lot of rain, overnight rain, morning rain, but it's time to play cricket and bone-dry conditions as always. Well covered, and we are ready to go. The pitch, well, it's starting to take turn. It's starting to bring in those variables in. Now, when I have a closer look, why it's going to get dangerous for the Sri Lankan batters is this area out there. That's for the off-spinner. Now this one here is for the left-armer. Then you also see these cracks opening. We didn't see that at Galle, but here it happens. Now look at what we saw yesterday when the ball turns and bounces. There was a slight explosion. With the heat beating down on this pitch like this, there's going to be a lot of wear and tear. Scoreboard pressure, turn, bounce, the fast bowlers from the other end. It's going to be very, very hard. Three spinners will keep coming at you, and there are plenty to work with out here. Well, Sri Lanka, can they dig in?

Prasidh Krishna (before start of play) (1/2): [On the wicket of Udara] Yeah, I think it was, there’s something in the pitch, of course. Maybe stopped a little bit. There was a bit of seam, and I think credit goes to Jaiswal for the catch that he took. It was an exceptional one. We have been putting in some effort on the field in practice, so I think it just paid off. [On the importance of the slip cordon] 100%. I think 50% of the job is bowling the ball there, getting an edge, but 50% is taking it as well, and we have been pretty good at doing that. I think it's also doing the simple things right, which we have been doing well, and that's what shows.

Prasidh (2/2): [On his aggressive approach as a bowler] Yeah, I would like to say so. I mean, aggression can come out in different ways, and for me it is about what I'm doing when I'm bowling. It's very easy for people to get away or be distracted by what's happening in the pitch. There's too much happening, there's not too much happening, but I think the focus is still to come in and bowl those areas with full effort. [On his stock length and whether it is influenced by his height] Length is something that keeps changing with pitches that we play on. So we sit with analysts, coaches, and everything and decide on what's the kind of length that we want to be bowling on different surfaces. And yeah, natural length was something that I could say when I was not playing for the country, but when I'm here I need to be bowling every length that the team wants, and I'm trying to do that.
